thread:
Sophie: heads up — customer 'AcmePayments' opened an urgent ticket, started seeing intermittent 403s from Redwood Dedicated behind their managed L7 proxy after migration yesterday. Logs show token parse failures.

Ajay: any chance this is the same header-strip issue? which gateway are they using?

Sophie: they have an external corporate proxy that inserts SSO Authorization cookies and also a corporate L7 that rewrites to an Authorization header. Their Dedicated is behind our VPC-LB -> Istio ingress. They said it worked in hosted but broke after Dedicated cutover.

Maya: can you paste a repro curl from their side? even a redacted one.

Sophie: from their support:
```
curl -v -H "Host: api.acme.example" \
  -H "Cookie: SSO=opaquetoken123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer redacted1" \
  https://dedicated.redwood.internal/route
*   Trying 10.0.0.3...\n* Connected to dedicated.redwood.internal (10.0.0.3) port 443 (#0)\n< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n< content-type: application/json\n< x-request-id: req-abc-123\n{\"error\":\"token_parse_failed\"}
```

Sophie: but when they curl without the corporate proxy (single Authorization header) it works. Suspect the corporate L7 is adding a second Authorization header (one from cookie->header rewrite plus the original), resulting in multiple Authorization headers arriving at Envoy. Our auth library rejects on multiple headers.

Ajay: interesting. Envoy merges duplicate headers into a single comma-separated header by default, which breaks opaque tokens. Did they show the raw upstream headers?

Sophie: they captured upstream and saw: `Authorization: Bearer redacted1, Bearer redacted2` (two values concatenated). Token parser expects a single token and fails.

Maya: that would explain intermittent behavior — depends on ordering and which token gets merged first. Also could be size issues.

Ricardo: is there any Istio or Envoy config that can be adjusted quickly? Maybe a header rewrite to prefer the last Authorization or drop duplicates?

Ajay: quick mitigation options:
- add an Envoy Lua filter at the ingress to coalesce and pick the last non-empty Bearer token and set Authorization to that
- set `preserve_external_request_id`? not relevant here
- configure the corporate L7 to stop adding Authorization if cookie present (customer action)
- add a small middleware in our Dedicated proxy that picks first/last header

Maya: can we reproduce locally with curl by sending two Authorization headers?

Sophie: yes repro:
```
# simulate corporate L7 sending two headers
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer aaaa" -H "Authorization: Bearer bbbb" https://staging-dedicated.redwood.internal/route
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n{\"error\":\"token_parse_failed\"}
```

Ajay: ok repro confirmed. Quick patch we shipped in an emergency a few quarters ago was an EnvoyFilter that normalizes Authorization like:
```
# pseudo-Istio EnvoyFilter lua snippet
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local h = request_handle:headers()
  local auth_vals = h:get("authorization")
  if type(auth_vals) == "table" and #auth_vals > 1 then
    -- pick the last bearer token
    local pick = auth_vals[#auth_vals]
    h:replace("authorization", pick)
  end
end
```

Maya: do we have that filter deployed for any customers right now?

Ricardo: we have it as an optional snippet for a few enterprise accounts but not enabled globally due to subtle header semantics.

Sophie: support asks for a recommended rollback/workaround they can push to Acme: 1) ask their L7 team to stop synthesizing Authorization if one exists, or 2) enable our Envoy Lua normalization on their Dedicated ingress (we can push as a config change in Private control plane), or 3) have them use X-Forwarded-Authorization instead and we map it server-side.

Ajay: I'd prefer 2) as a short-term fix we can flip in control plane for that customer only. We'll need a small CHANGE and a canary because it touches auth path.

Oncall-Bot: incident 2026-03-15-ACME-AUTH created and assigned to Ajay, priority P1 -> P2 after workaround plan proposed. Link: https://incidents.redwood/2026-03-15-ACME-AUTH

Ajay: I'll draft the EnvoyFilter, test on staging, and then roll to Acme's dedicated namespace. ETA 90m for staging test.

Maya: also flag eng-security — this touches auth headers; need security review before we apply long-term. @security please ack.

Sophie: customer happy with the plan, they provided emergency access window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC.

Ricardo: follow up checklist for post-mitigation:
- confirm logs show single Authorization header upstream
- run token-parser regression tests (we have unit tests)
- add telemetry to count duplicates to detect other customers
- docs note about multiple Authorization headers and proxies

Sophie: thanks all — Ajay, ping here when you have the staging filter. :thumbsup:

Ajay: will do, pushing sandbox now.

InfraBot: deploy request queued: changeset cs-98765 -> staging (envoy-filter-normalize-auth). Owner: Ajay.

Ajay: staging test passed, token parse now returns 200 with two incoming headers. Preparing canary to Acme's namespace.

Sophie: excellent. I'll update support and the customer.

Maya: long-term we should add a validation rule in our control plane to warn when multiple Authorization headers are observed for a customer Dedicated namespace. Filing a ticket.

Sophie: ticket filed: RED-3456. Closing thread once canary is healthy.
